text:
alex: seeing intermittent tail latency spikes for /generate in eu-west1 starting ~204s ago. pods are Pending due to GPU node provisioning delay, HPA didn't kick fast enough because external metric (qps_per_pod) was stale.

maria: confirmed — Prometheus scrape lag was 45s at the time, external metric adapter returned old values so HPA thought pods healthy.

jin: is CA not scaling? any events on nodepool? can you paste kubectl describe hpa and nodes?

alex: here are the relevant bits:
```
kubectl get hpa nlp-inference -o yaml
metrics:
- type: External
  external:
    metric:
      name: qps_per_pod
    target:
      type: AverageValue
      averageValue: "5"
```
CA events show "need 4 nodes, but quota exceeded" and a few "failed to provision GPU: no capacity" in eu-west1.

infra-oncall: alerted GCP quotas + spare GPU capacity in eu-west1 is low (regional stockout window). We can try spinning up a different nodepool in europe-west4 or use preemptible burst pool.

sam: quick mitigation: reduce HPA target to 3 qps and lower stabilizationWindowSeconds, that should create more pods earlier. downside: more pods => more GPU node requests => potential longer provisioning backlog + cost.

maria: alternative short-term: enable a small overprovisioned daemonset (node-prewarm) that creates 2 warm GPU nodes with a taint `prewarm=true:NoSchedule` and use pod tolerations for burstable pods. cheaper than reserved if we make them preemptible.

jin: another angle: make HPA use combined metrics (cpu + external) so CPU increases will trigger sooner even when external metric adapter lags. Also fix Prometheus scrape latency (we saw scrape jitter in the prometheus logs).

sre-bot: [ALERT] external-metric-adapter lag > 30s for 5m — triggering incident playbook 'ext-metric-lag'.

infra-oncall: I'm going to run a targeted scale command to add 2 nodes to the warm-pool in eu-west1:
```
gcloud container node-pools update warm-gpu-pool --cluster=redwood-prod --num-nodes=4 --region=eu-west1
```
Will monitor CA events and kube-scheduler pending queue.

alex: thanks. also let's avoid changing VPA for now — VPA + HPA is messy with resource requests. We should coordinate a follow-up playbook: 1) fix adapter scrape cadence, 2) add short-lived prewarm pool, 3) temporarily relax HPA downscale and target, 4) request quota bump in eu-west1.

sam: noted, cost owners — prewarm pool with preemptibles estimated +$1.2k/day, cc @finance.

maria: filing a quick runbook PR now with commands and rollback steps. will tag infra-oncall for execution window.

alex: OK, we'll watch for CA events and latency. ping me if pending pods > 50 for more than 2m :thumbsup:
